t: There is no church on this spot now. St Bartholomew-by-the-Exchange stood on Bartholomew Lane, off Threadneedle Street, and is recorded from the 13th century. The Great Fire of London destroyed it in 1666, and Sir Christopher Wren rebuilt it, as one of the 52 City churches he was given to rebuild. That rebuilt church was demolished in 1840. Among those buried here were the soldier Sir James Wilford, who commanded at the Siege of Haddington, and Joyce Barrett.
